items.headline: Stocks stay firm into big-tech earnings; I couldn't confirm Wednesday's close
items.note: CNBC's Oct 20 wrap said the S&P 500 notched a three-day win streak and the Nasdaq rose about 1% as SpaceX and Tesla rallied. Tesla and other tech names report this week, so Thursday's open depends on those results. Sources conflicted on Wednesday's exact index levels, so I'm leaving them out.

items.headline: Boston Fed's Collins says another rate hike is likely before year-end
items.note: The Fed raised rates a quarter point to 3.75%-4.00% in September. Collins backs further increases, and several officials signal the next hike is more likely in December than at the Oct 27-28 meeting. Higher rates matter for stock valuations and for the cost of borrowing.

items.headline: OpenAI's models come to Google Cloud
items.note: GPT models will be in Google Cloud's model garden and, in the coming weeks, its Antigravity coding tool. That puts OpenAI on all three big clouds, so you can use its models inside whichever cloud a company already runs.

items.headline: Tesla beats Q3 estimates even as car sales fall
items.note: Per CNBC, adjusted EPS was $0.48 vs. $0.43 expected and revenue $28.05B vs. $27.9B, with automotive revenue down 3%. The stock reportedly dropped more than 3% after hours. I couldn't open the article, so these figures come from the search summary.

items.headline: TSMC posts record Q3 on AI demand, yet shares fell
items.note: Forbes reports Q3 revenue of $46.72B with a 66.4% gross margin, and guidance of up to $54.3B for Q4. Strong results can still lead to selling when expectations are very high.

items.headline: Intel rebounds on a JPMorgan upgrade despite new chip export limits
items.note: The stock fell from a September high of about $127 to below $90 before the upgrade lifted it. Export restrictions on semiconductor technology are a continuing risk for chipmakers.

items.headline: Data scientist job growth is still projected to be strong
items.note: Recruiter reports cite a US Bureau of Labor Statistics projection of about 34% growth in data scientist jobs from 2024 to 2034. Postings now often ask for LLM and AI-pipeline skills. These are vendor summaries, not new data.

learn.explain: Market cap is the total value the stock market puts on a company: share price times the number of shares outstanding. A company with 1 billion shares at $50 each has a $50 billion market cap. It measures size, not how much cash the company has. When Intel's stock fell from about $127 to under $90, its market cap shrank by roughly the same percentage, even though the business itself didn't change overnight. Market cap is also how indexes like the S&P 500 weight companies, so bigger companies move the index more.
learn.try: Look up Intel's current share count and multiply it by its price to estimate its market cap.
